method.data: IRSA cutouts (2.4', 23 px) of every SPHEREx DR1/QR3 image listed by IRSA MOST, centred on MOST's predicted position; centroid within 1.5 px; 2 px aperture with the core's 1.033 aperture correction; sigma-clipped median background in a 4-9 px annulus; points with a mask bit (incl. OVERFLOW/NONLINEAR = saturation) within 2 px are dropped.
method.geometry: JPL Horizons, geocentre (location 500): SPHEREx is in low Earth orbit, < 1e-4 au away, negligible for main-belt asteroids. Interpolated from a 12 h ephemeris.
method.model: flux = reflected + NEATM thermal. Reflected: CALSPEC solar model x H-G phase function x p(lambda) D^2 with pv D^2 fixed by H (D = 1329/sqrt(pv) 10^-H/5) and p(lambda)/pv linear in lambda. NEATM: emissivity 0.9, Bond albedo q pv with q = 0.290 + 0.684 G. Fit over 2.2-5.05 um excluding 2.65-3.45 um; error floor 5% for rotation and calibration; 4-sigma clipping (blends, cosmic rays).
method.eta: adopted: the free fit (one D, one eta per visit) when every eta has sigma < 0.15 and lies in 0.6-2.0; otherwise eta fixed at 1.0 (close to the NEOWISE/IRAS/AKARI average of 0.8-1.0 for large main-belt asteroids) with one D per visit, combined as the mean of ln D; the error adds half the visit-to-visit spread. SPHEREx sees an asteroid near quadrature: the morning side in one visit and the warmer afternoon side six months later, which NEATM cannot model. The 3.8-5 um data sit on the Wien tail, where D and eta are degenerate, so the free eta often runs to its bounds. Both fits are kept (fit_eta_free, fit_eta_fixed) and summarised separately.
method.published: JPL SBDB phys_par (the adopted IRAS, NEOWISE or AKARI value; see D_ref/pv_ref).

band_3um_control.control_types: S, M, X, L, K (SBDB spec_B, else spec_T)

published.D_ref: Shepard et al. (2021), The Planetary Science Journal 2, 125
